title: Proactive quality ignition for model version locks
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Upgrading or pinning models (catalog or tenant-locked) currently relies on ad-hoc eval runs and manual QA. Several production incidents in Q4 highlighted missed regressions when configuration diffs (tokenization changes, temperature defaults, quantization profile swaps) were not included in automated checks. Goal: Build an automated, tenant-aware eval trigger system that fires targeted synthetic checks and prioritized smoke suites whenever a model version is pinned or upgraded in the catalog or a customer tenant. The system should be cost-aware, support tenant priority overrides, include fast preflight checks plus more comprehensive background probes, and provide clear pass/fail signals tied to rollout automation (canary/rollback).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A pin/upgrade event (catalog or tenant) triggers an eval job submission automatically within 2 minutes of the change.
2) Triggered job selects probe sets based on the delta metadata (model architecture change, tokenizer, quantization profile, config diffs) and tenant priority.
3) Fast preflight (<= 30s median) smoke returns a pass/fail signal that can gate automatic promotion.
4) Background fidelity probes run scaled by tenant budget and sampling policy and post results within 24 hours.
5) Metrics emitted: pass_rate, delta_score, regression_severity, cost_estimate, triggered_by, tenant_id, catalog_id.
6) Rollout integration: when preflight fails, a canary is aborted and an auto-rollback ticket is created with a link to the failing probe set.
7) Feature flags exist to disable customer-triggered evals per-tenant and to enable expanded probes for high-value customers.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (MVP): wire pin/upgrade webhook from Catalog service to Eval Orchestrator; implement lightweight preflight probe set chooser that maps common diffs (quantization change, tokenizer bump, model size change) to 5-7 smoke prompts; add tenant priority and budget lookup; emit events to observability pipeline.
Phase 2: extend chooser with fingerprint diffing for tokenizer and schema, integrate sampling controller for background probes, connect results to Rollout service for automatic canary gating, add queue/backpressure handling for high-volume pin spikes.
Phase 3: polish UX in Console (per-pin eval timeline, per-tenant budget controls), add SLA/alerting on stuck probes, implement cost caps and auto-throttling.
Key deliverables: webhook contract, smoke probe library v1, preflight API, orchestration runbook, docs page for tenant controls.
observability_and_alerting: Emit structured events to Metrics: eval.triggered, eval.preflight.duration_ms, eval.preflight.result, eval.background.duration_ms, eval.background.regressions_found, eval.cost. Integrate with Console dashboard: per-catalog and per-tenant eval summary, regression heatmap, historical delta trends. Alerts: P0 if preflight fails for >3 distinct tenants in 1 hour for same catalog change; P1 if probe queue latency > 10 minutes for >95th percentile requests. Include tracer spans for webhook->orchestrator->runner path.
cost_budgeting_controls: Support three budget controls: tenant-monthly-eval-budget, per-pin-cost-cap, sample-rate-throttle. Default conservative budgets for free-tier tenants (fast preflight only). Allow premium tenants to opt-in for expanded fidelity probes. Orchestrator will estimate cost before scheduling and decline/queue probes that exceed budget; decline reasons included in webhook response.
rollout_strategy: Start with internal catalog pins (redwood-internal) for 2 weeks to validate end-to-end flow. Next enable a small cohort of opt-in customers (5 tenants) with varying traffic patterns. Monitor cost and regression hit rate, iterate on probe selector. After stable results and dashboard UX, flip on for all catalog pins and offer tenant opt-in via Console. Provide a kill-switch and per-tenant disable flag during ramp.
